Love of God
LUHV uhv GOD
noun (divine attribute)
From Old English lufu, affection, rendering Hebrew ahabah and Greek agape; the settled, willing good of God toward His creatures and, peculiarly, toward His elect.

Biblical Definition

The love of God is His eternal, self-moved goodness, by which He wills and works the good of His creatures, and most of all the everlasting salvation of His elect. We must distinguish His general benevolence, by which He maketh His sun to rise on the evil and the good (Matt 5:45), from His special, electing, saving love set upon His people before the foundation of the world. This saving love is not occasioned by anything lovely in us, for "God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us" (Rom 5:8). It is electing love: "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world" (Eph 1:4-5). It is redeeming love: "In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him" (1 John 4:9). And it is propitiating love, for herein is love, that He sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins (1 John 4:10). This love is no soft sentimentalism that overlooks sin; it is holy love that satisfies justice at the cross. This dictionary confesses that the love of God is sovereign, particular, and unbreakable, the fountain of election and the ground of all our hope.

Webster 1828 Definition

The love of God is His self-moved goodness toward His creatures, and chiefly His electing, redeeming affection set upon the elect. It is distinguished from mere benevolence to all by its saving particularity. It is holy, not sentimental, satisfying justice at the cross.

expand to see more

LOVE OF GOD, noun. The eternal and gracious disposition of God to will and work the good of His creatures, and supremely the salvation of His elect.

It is distinguished into a general benevolence shown to all, and a special saving love set upon His chosen.

"But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us" (Rom 5:8).

It requires that we love Him in return with heart, soul, mind, and strength; it forbids that we mistake His love for indulgence of sin.

It is the spring of election, the gift of the Son, and the seal of an everlasting covenant that cannot fail.

Key Scripture

John 3:16 — "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life."

Rom 5:8 — "But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us."

Eph 1:4-5 — "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will."

1 John 4:9 — "In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him."

Modern Corruption

The age recasts the love of God as an unconditional, undiscriminating affirmation that never judges and never condemns, severing love from holiness and wrath.

expand to see more

Modern religion loves to say "God is love" while emptying the word of its biblical content. It makes divine love a blanket approval of every man as he is, a love that demands no repentance and tolerates every sin, so that hell becomes unthinkable and the cross becomes unnecessary. But Scripture binds love to holiness: the same God who is love is also a consuming fire, and His love for the elect was purchased by the pouring out of His wrath upon His Son. A love that will not satisfy justice is not the love of the living God but an idol of sentiment.

Recover the holy, electing, particular love that runs through the covenant of grace. God set His love upon a people, gave His Son to die for them, and will bring every one of them home. This love is tender beyond telling, yet it never winks at sin; it slays sin at the cross that the beloved may be made holy. To know oneself loved with such love is the strongest motive to godliness and the surest comfort in affliction.

Hebrew Roots

Behind love lie Hebrew ahabah and Greek agape, the willing, self-giving good of God toward His people.

expand to see more

Hebrew ahabah, love, is rooted in covenant choice, as the LORD loved Israel not for her greatness (Deut 7:7-8).

Greek agape denotes a deliberate, self-giving good will, supremely shown in the gift of the Son.

The verb agapao in John 3:16 governs the giving of the only begotten Son for sinners.

Old English lufu supplies our word love, but Scripture fills it with electing and redeeming content.

The summit of the word is 1 John 4:10, where love is defined by propitiation, not by sentiment.

Usage

"The love of God in election is the deep spring from which every mercy in our salvation flows."

"He warned them never to set the love of God against the wrath of God, for both meet at the cross."

"Her dying comfort was the love of God, sealed in the blood of the everlasting covenant."
